object_description: continuous low-rise perimeter frontage enclosing a green public garden
design_condition: The built frontage defines the block perimeter while varying its height toward residential and villa neighborhoods, enclosing a central public garden and connecting the school through a soft-mobility network.

positive.statement: The continuous frontage is successfully integrated through its low height and street-side gardens.
The dimensions of the housing adapt judiciously to existing and future neighborhoods.
The school’s central position makes it visible from all sides and connects it to the different paths.
The reception and transition space provides natural security for the exterior areas.
The simple and functional program arrangement gives the younger classes a direct relationship with the garden and playground.
The circulation areas are pleasant and well dimensioned, with views toward the garden and old town.
The central breathing space supports small-group activities and brings natural light into the building.
The orientation of the classrooms is good.
The use of wood as covering and structure makes sense in the garden setting and supports rapid dry execution and energy efficiency.

negative.statement: The jury regrets that the existing plane trees were not integrated into the concept.
The northern volume could have included more breakthroughs and permeabilities for the neighborhood and future residents.
The niche-based changing-room layout is appreciated, but the principle is not applied systematically.
The desired relationships between certain premises are not always achieved.
The proximity of the northwestern classroom to housing is questionable.
